html:
Work on the Taj Mahal, the white marble tomb at Agra on the Yamuna River, began in 1632. The Mughal emperor Shah Jahan built it for his wife Mumtaz Mahal, who had died in childbirth the year before.

The tomb itself was finished in about 1643, and the whole complex of gardens, mosque, guest hall and gateway around 1653. Tens of thousands of workers took part. The chief architect is usually named as Ustad Ahmad Lahauri.

It drew on earlier Mughal tombs, above all Humayun's Tomb in Delhi, but changed them in key ways:

  • It is faced in white marble from Makrana in Rajasthan, not red sandstone.
  • The tomb stands at the far end of the garden, by the river, not at its centre.
  • Flowers of inlaid stone, a craft called pietra dura, cover the walls.

Shah Jahan was buried beside his wife in 1666. The Taj became a World Heritage Site in 1983 and is the best known building in India, a peak of Mughal architecture.
